_headline: NO BUILD BROKE THE CLIMB. All four climb identically. The variable was MY DRIVE DIRECTION, and my 'the arcs never engage in either direction' was an over-generalisation from a leftward-only run.
_protocol: identical every time: grounded-asserted at x1000 (settles to y557, y_vel 0, engine row 34, plane A), then gsp +$600 with sustained held RIGHT. Max climb = minimum y reached.

results.verdict: FULL CIRCUIT — up the right arc, over the crown, down the left

results.build: master e99b9d54 (direction gate + floor fan + chords)
results.verdict: IDENTICAL — the loop is NOT broken on master

_correction.my_claim: 'the arcs do not pick up a ground-level runner in either direction' (f478fe25) and 'stop testing crossover rules until a drive climbs'.
_correction.what_is_true: RIGHTWARD climbs on every build including master, to the same pixel and the same angle. Only LEFTWARD does not climb. I measured one direction and wrote 'either direction'.
_correction.why_leftward_not_climbing_is_EXPECTED: travelling west, the first arc met is the RIGHT arc, solid only on plane B. On plane A without a crossing there is nothing to climb. That is the hub's original geometry, and it means leftward non-climb is a CONSEQUENCE of the crossover question rather than evidence about it.

_what_this_re_opens: the crossover comparison is live again and was never invalidated by a broken loop. Under the direction rule leftward correctly refuses TO_B and therefore cannot climb; under the plane-keyed rule it should cross at the bottom mark and climb the right arc on B. That comparison now needs re-running from a VALID grounded start (x1200), which my earlier x1600 attempt was not.
_owed: aurora's boundary prediction (ground holds to x1279, fails from x1280, because the block/map layer never placed cols 160+) is UNTESTED. Two drives.
